pages.title: Introduction
pages.content:
## Welcome to the Wildlife

Walk a little slower and look around. Thirty new animals now live in Iekcorbar, next to the cows and sheep you already know. They are shy and rare, and each one has its own home: red deer in the forests, mallards on the river, fireflies over the swamp at night, crabs on the beach, elephants and zebras on the savanna - and in the bamboo thickets and snowy woods, the tanuki, the red-crowned crane, the golden koi and troops of macaques. New since spring: roos hopping the plains, an ostrich that outruns you, crocodiles that are logs with opinions, napping koalas, molehills (and once, a mole), rhinos in the dust, penguin colonies on the ice, a blow out in the deep ocean - orca - and red-bellied piranha shoals in the warm shallows, while scarlet macaws scream over the jungle canopy.

This is not about catching or fighting. It is about **finding, watching and recording**, like a naturalist with a field journal. No mods needed.

### What you will do

* **Explore.** Different biomes, different animals. Some come out only by day, some only at night, snails like rain.
* **Watch.** Look at an animal through a spyglass for a moment and it is written in your Field Journal.
* **Collect.** Each species is an advancement in the Wildlife tab, and some animals have a rare colouring that counts as a special find.
* **Be gentle.** Deer run if you walk up to them, bears sleep at night and are calm until hurt. Learn how each animal behaves.

### How the pages are organised

**Wildlife** explains the journal and the advancements. **Species** lists every animal and where to look for it. **Breeding and Babies** explains how to raise young animals, and **Statues** how to build a stone version of any animal.

### Good to know first

* Nothing from the normal game was removed or replaced. Wildlife is only added.
* Animals are scarce on purpose. If you see nothing, keep exploring and try another time of day.
* A **name tag** keeps an animal in place, otherwise it wanders off when nobody is near.

### Start here

1. Craft a spyglass (copper ingot and amethyst shard).
2. Read [Wildlife](/wiki?page=wildlife) to see how the journal works.
3. Pick an animal from [Species](/wiki?page=wildlife-species) and go and find it.

pages.title: Wildlife
pages.content:
## Wildlife - shy animals to find and record

Iekcorbar's countryside has new animals living next to the familiar ones: deer in the forests, mallards on the rivers, fireflies over the swamps at night, crabs scuttling along the beach - and in the east, tanuki at dusk, cranes standing in the reeds, koi gliding under the surface and macaques chattering in the trees. They are **rare and shy**, and each species only lives in its own kind of place. Nothing vanilla was removed - cows, pigs and sheep are all still there.

### How it works

1. **Get a spyglass** (copper + amethyst shard, as in vanilla).
2. **Find an animal** in the right biome. Some only come out by day, fireflies only at night, and snails like the rain.
3. **Watch it through the spyglass** for about a second. It goes into your **Field Journal** and you get an advancement.
4. **Read your journal** with **/wildlife journal**, or craft a **Field Journal** (book + feather + wheat seeds) and right-click it. Species you haven't found yet show a hint.

### Rare looks

Now and then an animal has a rare colouring - an albino deer, a blue morpho butterfly, a capybara wearing a yuzu. Spotting one gives its own (hidden) advancement and a mark in your journal.

### Advancements

Open the advancement screen and look for the **Wildlife** tab: one advancement per species, one per rare look, and milestones for 5 species, 10 species, every species, your first rare find and 5 rare finds.

### Behaviour worth knowing

* **Deer and lizards** run when you come close - sneak to get near.
* **Hedgehogs and snails** curl up or hide in their shell; **tortoises** pull in their head and legs.
* **Brown bears** are calm until you hurt them, sleep at night and eat sweet berries.
* **Wild boars** charge when they feel cornered.
* **Capybaras** sometimes give a duck or a songbird a ride.
* **Lizards** can drop their tail when hit (it grows back). **Crabs** sometimes drop a claw: hold a **Crab Claw** in your off hand to reach one block further.
* A **name tag** keeps an animal around; unnamed wildlife wanders off when nobody is near. So does a **lead**: an animal you put on a lead stays.
* Only adult bears and boars ever fight back. Every other animal is harmless, and so are their young.
* **Young animals** exist too, and you can raise them: see [Breeding and Babies](/wiki?page=wildlife-breeding).

See [Wildlife Species](/wiki?page=wildlife-species) for where each animal lives.

* [Koi](/wiki?page=wildlife-species-koi)
* [Japanese Macaque](/wiki?page=wildlife-species-japanese-macaque)

The **African Elephant** is the biggest animal around and the **Plains Zebra** always walks in a group. Both have a rare look too: a white elephant and a golden zebra. From the east come four more: the night-wandering **Tanuki** (rarely seen, charcoal-black on lucky nights), the stately **Red-Crowned Crane** that stays with its partner for life, the **Koi** gliding just under the surface (the all-gold one is the famous Golden Koi), and noisy troops of **Japanese Macaques** in the bamboo and snowy woods.

And everywhere their own little rumours: a fresh **molehill** in the lawn means a **Mole** has been working below - see one of them and you are lucky. **Penguins** bray like donkeys on the ice, **koalas** sleep the day away, and a **crocodile** is exactly as still as it looks. Out in the deep ocean, an **Orca** surfaces so rarely that nobody plans on it; near the jungle water, a shimmering shoal of **Piranhas** is a reminder not to swim there hungry, and the **Scarlet Macaw** overhead will happily repeat back whatever you said about it.

Animals are scarce on purpose: if you don't see one, keep exploring - and try a different time of day.

pages.title: Breeding and Babies
pages.content:
## Breeding and babies

Every animal can have young - even the bees and the songbirds. Raising them is slow on purpose.


* [How to breed](/wiki?page=wildlife-breeding-how-to-breed)
* [What to feed](/wiki?page=wildlife-breeding-what-to-feed)
* [Babies](/wiki?page=wildlife-breeding-babies)
* [Keep a baby small](/wiki?page=wildlife-breeding-keep-a-baby-small)
* [Keeping your animals](/wiki?page=wildlife-breeding-keeping-your-animals)
* [Good to know](/wiki?page=wildlife-breeding-good-to-know)

pages.title: How to breed
pages.content:
1. **Right-click an adult with its food** (table below). Hearts appear: it is in love for 30 seconds.
2. Do the same to **a second animal of the same kind** within a few blocks.
3. The two walk to each other and **a baby appears**. Both parents need about 5 minutes before they can have another one.

If a lot of the same animal is already close by, the game says it is **too crowded** and nothing happens. That keeps farms small.

Back to [Breeding and Babies](/wiki?page=wildlife-breeding)

pages.title: What to feed
pages.content:
| Animal | Food |
|---|---|
| Red Deer | wheat, apples or carrots |
| Brown Bear | sweet berries, salmon or honey |
| Wild Boar | carrots, potatoes or beetroot |
| Mallard, Songbird | seeds |
| Monarch Butterfly | small flowers |
| Firefly | glow berries |
| Garden Snail | dried kelp or seagrass |
| Hedgehog | mushrooms |
| Capybara | melon slices or sugar cane |
| Tortoise | seagrass |
| Wall Lizard | spider eyes |
| Shore Crab | cod or kelp |
| Emperor Dragonfly | sugar |
| African Elephant | wheat, sugar cane or apples |
| Plains Zebra | wheat or hay bales |
| Tanuki | sweet berries or apples |
| Red-Crowned Crane | seeds or a fish |
| Koi | kelp or a piece of bread |
| Japanese Macaque | apples, carrots or potatoes |
| Red Kangaroo | wheat, hay or carrots |
| Common Ostrich | seeds |
| Siamese Crocodile | fish or a piece of beef |
| Koala | leaves or apples |
| European Mole | spider eyes (it really eats grubs) |
| White Rhinoceros | wheat, hay or melon |
| Emperor Penguin | fish |
| Orca | a big fish |
| Red-bellied Piranha | any raw meat |
| Scarlet Macaw | seeds or cocoa beans |

Back to [Breeding and Babies](/wiki?page=wildlife-breeding)

pages.title: Babies
pages.content:
A baby is **half the size**, with a big head, and it is harmless - even a bear cub or a boar piglet. It grows up after about 20 minutes. Feeding a baby its food makes it grow a little faster.

Back to [Breeding and Babies](/wiki?page=wildlife-breeding)

pages.title: Keep a baby small
pages.content:
Give a baby a **golden dandelion** and it **stays a baby**. Give it another golden dandelion and it starts growing again. A baby kept small is yours: it stays where you left it, even when nobody is around.

Back to [Breeding and Babies](/wiki?page=wildlife-breeding)

pages.title: Keeping your animals
pages.content:
Wild animals wander off when nobody is near. A **name tag**, a **lead**, or a golden dandelion (for babies) keeps an animal for good. Perfect for a zoo.

Back to [Breeding and Babies](/wiki?page=wildlife-breeding)

pages.title: Good to know
pages.content:
* A baby born next to its parents looks like them. Rare parents have a good chance of a rare baby.
* A grown-up that was on a lead slips out of it and the lead drops to the ground.
* Young animals now and then show up on their own in a bigger group.

Back to [Breeding and Babies](/wiki?page=wildlife-breeding)

pages.title: Statues
pages.content:
## Animal statues

Every animal can be placed as a **true-size statue**, in three versions: the animal, its **rare look** and a **baby**. They are decoration for your zoo or garden.


* [Crafting](/wiki?page=wildlife-statues-crafting)
* [Placing and moving](/wiki?page=wildlife-statues-placing-and-moving)

pages.title: Crafting
pages.content:
Craft them on a crafting table, no pattern needed. Use stone and the **item that animal drops** (the same one shown on its advancement):

| Statue | Ingredients |
|---|---|
| Adult | 3 stone + the animal's item |
| Baby | 2 stone + the animal's item |
| Rare | 3 stone + the animal's item + 1 amethyst shard |

For example a deer statue is 3 stone and leather.

Back to [Statues](/wiki?page=wildlife-statues)

pages.title: Placing and moving
pages.content:
* Right-click a block with the statue to place it. It turns to face you.
* **Hit it a few times** to pick it up again.
* The elephant statue is three blocks tall, so leave some room.

Statues stand still; the real animals are found in the wild. They go well with the **Zoo** props: fences, gates, troughs and info boards.

Back to [Statues](/wiki?page=wildlife-statues)
